Bonus Feat.description: Upon reaching 2nd level, the spellsword furthers his expertise and receives a bonus feat. This feat must be selected from either the metamagic feat category or the fighter bonus feat list.

Channel Spell.description: Beginning at 4th level, the spellsword gains the ability to infuse any spell he can cast into his melee weapon. Doing so requires a move action and expends the prepared spell or spell slot as though the spell had been cast normally. The stored spell takes effect on the next creature the spellsword hits with that weapon (the target may still attempt saving throws and benefit from spell resistance as usual). Regardless of whether the spell would ordinarily affect an area or function as a ray, it only strikes the single target hit. Once the spell discharges, the weapon can receive a new spell. Only one weapon can hold a channeled spell at a time. Any spell stored in a weapon that goes unused for 8 hours is lost.

Ignore Spell Failure.description: Starting at 1st level, the spellsword's dedicated training in combining magic with martial technique begins to bear fruit. As an extraordinary ability, he reduces the arcane spell failure chance imposed by armor he wears. This reduction begins at 10% and progressively rises to 30% as he advances in level. The spellsword simply subtracts the listed percentage from his total arcane spell failure chance. For example, a 1st-level spellsword wearing scale mail and a small shield (which would normally impose a 30% failure chance) would only suffer a 20% chance of spell failure.

Multiple Channel Spell.description: At 10th level, the spellsword becomes capable of storing two spells simultaneously in his melee weapon, spending a move action to channel each one. When the spellsword lands a hit, both stored spells discharge against the target in the sequence they were placed into the weapon. Saving throws and spell resistance function normally for each spell. Using this ability expends two of the spellsword's five daily uses of channel spell.

Spells per Day.description: At each odd-numbered spellsword level (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th), the character gains additional spells per day as though he had also advanced one level in whichever arcane spellcasting class he belonged to before entering this prestige class. This progression improves his effective caster level and spells per day but does not confer any other class benefits (such as undead turning, bonus metamagic feats, item creation feats, or similar features). A character who previously had levels in more than one arcane casting class must choose which class receives the benefit for the purpose of calculating spells per day.

This reduction starts at 10%and gradually increases to 30%, as shown on the class table. A spellsword subtracts the given percentage value from his total spell failure chance, if any.
